chunks: He said: Abul Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Hasan reported to me from his father, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Musa ibn Bakr, who said: Someone who heard Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad, peace be upon them both, narrated to me that he was saying:
"The one who acts without insight is like one traveling upon a mirage in a plain — the speed of his travel only increases his distance."

key_terms.العامل: The worker/actor — one who performs religious deeds and worldly actions
key_terms.بصيرة: Insight (basira) — spiritual discernment and understanding that guides action; deeper than mere knowledge
key_terms.سراب: Mirage (sarab) — an illusion in the desert that appears to be water but leads the thirsty further astray; a Quranic image (24:39)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about acting without understanding or insight?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (as) uses a powerful Quranic image to teach that action without understanding is counterproductive. Drawing on the imagery of Quran 24:39, he compares the uninformed worker to a thirsty traveler chasing a mirage in the desert: the faster he moves, the farther he gets from his goal. This hadith was narrated through an unnamed intermediary, emphasizing the importance of basira (spiritual insight) as a prerequisite for meaningful religious practice.

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 11. He said: Abul Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Hasan reported to me from his father, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Musa ibn Bakr, who said: Someone who heard from Abu Abdillah Ja’far ibn Muhammad (as) reported to me that he said: "
One who acts without any understanding and vision, is like a person walking behind a mirage on a levelled desert, the faster he runs the farthest he ends up.
